# Stackra

> Stackra — the @stackra/* packages, apps and services, and how to work in the monorepo.

- [Introduction](/): What Stackra is and how this repository is organised.
- [Roadmap](/roadmap): The master delivery plan: phases, waves, the critical path, blocking decisions, spikes and milestones.
- [Quickstart](/quickstart): From a clean machine to a running console and docs site.
- [Development](/development): From a clean clone to a green pnpm verify, and the commands you use every day.
- [Repository structure](/guides/structure): Top-level layout and what belongs where.
- [Package categories](/guides/packages): packages/<category>/<name>: one level of category, packages flat inside it.
- [Tooling presets](/guides/tooling): The four config packages every member extends.
- [Commits and releases](/guides/workflow): Git hooks, conventional commits, changesets and secret scanning.
- [Definition of done](/guides/definition-of-done): What must be true before a change is done, each line tied to the check that enforces it.
- [Scaffolding](/guides/scaffolding): Create a member with pnpm new, what the templates replace, and how to move code with a script instead of by hand.
- [Console](/guides/console): Write a CLI command with @stackra/console: the Command class, its arguments and options, output, prompts, --json, themes and tests.
- [Member standards](/guides/standards): What every app, package and service must contain.
- [Dependency catalogs](/guides/catalogs): One version per dependency, declared once in pnpm-workspace.yaml.
- [Testing](/guides/testing): Tests live next to the code they prove.
- [Architecture map](/guides/architecture-map): Every member by tier, category and runtime, and the client calls between services, drawn from the repository.
- [Approvals](/build/approvals): Declare a second approver on an action: what the stage checks, who runs the call after the last vote, and what a service has to bind.
- [Contracts](/build/contracts): Every Stackra package's types-only ./contracts entry: which members have one, what the contracts batch added, and the asks for the rest.
- [Get access and install](/customers/install): Point your package manager at the Stackra registry, install the free @stackra packages, and add a licence token for @stackra-pro.
- [Support, versioning and end-of-life](/customers/support): How Stackra versions its packages, what 0.x means, how deprecations run, and the support terms.
- [Security overview](/customers/security): How Stackra isolates tenants, authorises calls, keeps audit evidence, protects keys and secrets, and proves where each package came from.
- [Data residency](/customers/residency): How a Stackra deployment keeps each tenant's data in its region: what never crosses a region, where backups and logs go, and what is not finished.
- [Changelog](/customers/changelog): Where each release's changes are recorded: per-package changelogs, GitHub releases and the registry.
- [API reference](/customers/packages): Every @stackra package: what it is for, its entry points, and links to its README and changelog.
- [Constitution](/constitution): The laws every contributor and agent follows. Laws outrank ADRs, and every law names the check that enforces it.
- [Boundaries](/constitution/boundaries): Tiers, dependency direction, the placement test, service ownership, and the rule that shared packages hold factories rather than values.
- [Secrets](/constitution/secrets): Two kinds of secret, two mechanisms, never a third. A human or the secret-manager inbox flow sets every value, and nobody reads one.
- [HTTP and events](/constitution/http-and-events): One endpoint per operation, authentication by default, verbs by idempotency, cursor lists, prefixed ids, idempotency keys and versioned events.
- [Security](/constitution/security): One authenticated principal per request, server-side authorization, audit, data classification and supply-chain controls.
- [Tenancy](/constitution/tenancy): Two-layer tenant isolation, where the tenant context comes from, the isolation tests every tenant-owned table needs, and the rules for the scope tree.
- [Delegation](/constitution/delegation): Claude decides, executors get self-contained briefs, git writes stay with the dispatcher, and review is by gates.
- [Architecture decisions](/adr): Why the repository looks the way it does.

- [ADR template](/adr/template): Copy this page, give it the next number, fill every section.
- [Member standards](/standards/members): What every app, package and service must contain, and which check enforces each rule.
- [Package standards](/standards/packages): The entries-first package shape, exports, barrels, and the provenance of copied code.
- [Repository structure](/standards/structure): The categories, kind folders, banned folders, file suffixes and test tiers every member follows, generated by stackra structure.
- [Service standards](/standards/services): The eight things a complete service must have, and what is checked today.
- [App standards](/standards/apps): Rules for the console, mobile, desktop and docs apps: leaves of the graph, build-time config, budgets, no fixtures in the build.
- [Code style](/standards/code-style): File contract, TSDoc, naming, one declaration per file, imports and typed errors.
- [Testing](/standards/testing): Where tests live, what a green run proves, fakes instead of secrets, and the end-to-end matrix.
- [Testing by file kind](/standards/testing-by-kind): Which test each kind of source file needs, and the file name that test takes. Must match the structure tables of @stackra/repo-checks.
- [Dependencies](/standards/dependencies): One version per dependency in catalogs, toolchain pins in mise.toml, install-script and licence gates.
- [Internationalisation and RTL](/standards/i18n-rtl): ICU messages with typed keys, locales defined by apps, and layout written in logical directions.
- [UI and accessibility](/standards/ui-and-accessibility): Reuse-first UI on the shared components, design tokens only, WCAG 2.2 AA, and how the accessibility review runs.
- [Stackra setup runbook](/runbooks/setup): Every account, where each secret name lives, the ordered setup steps and which ones only the owner can do. Names only.
- [Secrets](/runbooks/secrets): Two kinds of secret, two mechanisms: who sets a value, where it lives and how code or CI reads it.
- [Token rotation after exposure](/runbooks/token-rotation): What to do when a token reaches an agent transcript, a log or a terminal, and the guard that keeps process listings from printing injected secrets.
- [GitHub identities](/runbooks/github-identities): Which GitHub identity each actor uses, the bot commands that replace plain gh and git, and what the owner sets up.
- [CI](/runbooks/ci): One required check that runs pnpm verify, how to reproduce it locally with zero secrets, and what to do when CI is down.
- [Release](/runbooks/release): Changesets, the version-packages pull request, publishing to the Stackra registry through GitHub OIDC, prereleases, failures and recovery.
- [Mobile release](/runbooks/mobile-release): EAS builds, signs, submits and updates the Expo app; a human bootstraps the stores once.
- [Mobile onboarding](/runbooks/mobile-onboarding): One command takes a product's mobile app from nothing to store-ready; the owner does a few portal steps once.
- [Renovate](/runbooks/renovate): One shared dependency policy: one-day release age, SHA digests, no automerge, advisories bypass the wait.
- [Deploys](/runbooks/deploys): Agents prepare, the owner runs every deploy: staging first, then production from the same commit, and roll back by redeploying a recorded release.
- [Monitoring our Workers and the registry](/runbooks/monitoring): How npm.stackra.figentra.com, static.stackra.figentra.com and turbo.stackra.figentra.com are watched: Workers Logs, Better Stack uptime monitors and the status page, what the owner sets up first, and how the stack is applied from CI.
- [Test infrastructure (the testbed)](/runbooks/test-infrastructure): The shared test boxes every builder session uses: how jobs run, the disk guard, replacing a box, rebuilding the image, secrets, the fallback, cost, and the migration from the old ci-box fleet.
- [Runway](/runbooks/runway): How Stackra deploys: the runway files, the reusable provider workflows, the one deploy command, the secrets and vars sync, and what is not built yet.
- [Upgrade](/runbooks/upgrade): Checklists for toolchain, Expo SDK and preset upgrades.
- [Fresh machine](/runbooks/fresh-machine): Clone, install the pinned toolchain, log in, and let pnpm doctor tell you what is still missing.
- [Working with agents](/agents): How AI agents work in this repository: one .agents/ source, delegation to tiered subagents, and the gates that decide what merges.
- [Roster](/agents/roster): The agents that work in this repository: tier, model, whether they block, and what each owns.
- [Hooks](/agents/hooks): What each agent hook denies or reminds, how settings wire them, and how they are tested.
- [Skills](/agents/skills): Plugin skills, vendored skills, how to install them, and what is deliberately not vendored.
- [Knowledge-work plugins](/agents/plugins): The four Anthropic plugins every session has, what each is for, and where Stackra's own agents and skills take precedence.
- [Spec lifecycle](/agents/spec-lifecycle): How work that is worth specifying moves from idea to merged change with Figentra Flow: clarify before plan, a Linear issue per spec, and where a finding goes.
- [Concurrent sessions](/agents/concurrent-sessions): Working safely when several agent sessions share a clone: preconditions, ownership of a change, worktrees, and phased work.
- [Rules that don't rot](/agents/rules-that-dont-rot): Every rule names the check that fails when it breaks, and every vendored copy needs a drift check.
- [Markdown syntax](/writing/markdown): Headings, text formatting, lists and tables.
- [Code blocks](/writing/code): Syntax highlighting, titles, groups and line highlights.
- [Images and embeds](/writing/images): Pictures, light/dark variants and video.
- [Components](/writing/components): Callouts, cards, steps, tabs and accordions.
- [Navigation](/writing/navigation): Adding pages, groups and tabs in the DocsConfig.
- [Reusable snippets](/writing/reusable-snippets): Write a passage once and include it on many pages.
- [Site settings](/writing/settings): What each field of the DocsConfig controls.
- [Brand kit](/brand): Every Stackra brand file the docs app carries: logos, marks, app icons, favicons, icons, illustrations, patterns and splash marks.
